about.heading: Building real software, carefully.
paragraphs: I'm Farzan, a second-year Information Technology student at Matrusri Engineering College. I learn by building and shipping: BhuKosh, my Smart India Hackathon 2026 project, is a live land-record digitization system where every AI-extracted value must prove where it came from. WikiExplore, a reading portal for all 66 million Wikipedia articles, runs entirely on Wikimedia's public APIs.

What pulls me in is software that has to earn trust — document AI, validation, auditability — and I strengthen the CS fundamentals underneath it with a structured C and data-structures track. I care that the things I make actually run, and that what I claim about them can be checked.

projects.name: BhuKosh
projects.problem: Land records in India exist mostly as scans of handwritten registers, in multiple Indian scripts. Digitization demos stop at "the AI read the text" — but land records demand the harder question: can you trust what was read, and can you prove it?
projects.contribution: I designed and built the system end to end: the evidence-binding model that ties every extracted value to the exact pixels it was read from, the validation rules that catch impossible data before review, and the truth-assurance verdict computed from independently checkable signals — never the model's own opinion. The live app and OpenAPI-documented service are deployed and walkable in about a minute.
projects.design: OCR and document extraction feed a validation layer; human corrections loop back to teach the extractor. Every decision — machine or human — lands on a tamper-evident audit chain, so the final record carries its own justification.
projects.tradeoff: Automation versus accountability. A faster pipeline that can't show its work is useless for land records, so BhuKosh deliberately spends effort on evidence capture and audit rather than raw extraction speed.
projects.outcome: The system is live with a working app and documented API. The 60-second demo path — sign in as checker, open a pending record, click Evidence, check assurance — runs on the deployed service today.
projects.demoNote: Sign in as checker / checker-dev → open a pending record → click Evidence, then Check assurance.

projects.name: WikiExplore
projects.whatItIs: A live reading portal for all of Wikipedia — 66 million articles — that opens on today's real featured article.
projects.whyItExists: The original hackathon build shipped ~27 KB of hardcoded articles pretending to be a library. WikiExplore is the honest version: everything live, nothing canned.
projects.howItWorks: One Wikimedia feed call powers the home page — featured article of the day, most-read, on-this-day history, and news. The reader boots today's featured article, pulls live sections with a table of contents, weaves in cross-link previews, and merges each chapter's citations into real numbered footnotes. No database, no backend, no framework — restraint as a product decision, in ~4,240 lines of hand-written vanilla JS.
